ἐξάγγ-ελος , ὁ, ἡ,
A.messenger who brings out news from within: hence, one who betrays a secret, informer,
“ἐ. γίγνεται ὡς . .”
Th. 8.51
; “ἐ. γίγνεσθαί τινος”
Pl. Lg. 964e
, etc.
II. on the Greek stage, messenger who told what was doing in the house or behind the scenes (opp. ἄγγελος, who told news from a distance); first used by Aeschylus, Philostr. VS 1.9 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
